topic: A hand-rolled test stub must implement the WHOLE service interface, or a gated proof crashes before it proves anything
lesson: The selection-slice D-0008 proof crashed with 'this.resolver.canonicalPlant is not a function' because its fake resolver (selection-slice.db.test.ts:48) implemented only resolve(), while MisSelectionService.run() calls this.resolver.canonicalPlant(request.plant) first for the plant-scope check. The REAL SelectionResolverService implements it (selection-resolver.service.ts:53) — only the stub was partial, so the proof failed before exercising a single row and both the performance and security lenses blocked on it. FIX: type the stub against the ISelectionResolverService interface (backend/src/mapping/selection-resolver.interface.ts) so TypeScript rejects a partial implementation, and implement every member it declares — canonicalPlant, options and resolve. Principle: never hand-roll a loosely-typed stub for an interface that exists; bind it to the interface so adding a method to the service breaks the stub at compile time instead of at proof time.
source: selection-resolution review round 2 (performance + security P1 both on the partial stub; proof 15/16)
